title: Vanishing on infinitesimal layers gives neighbourhood lifts of fibre sections
statement: Let $f:Z\to S$ be a proper morphism [def-weil-proper-morphism] of schemes [def-pc-scheme], with $S$ Noetherian, that is, locally Noetherian [pqf-def-locnoeth] and quasi-compact [def-weil-pbc-quasi-compact-scheme]. Let $s\in S$ and let $E$ be an invertible $\mathcal O_Z$-module [def-sc-invertible-module]. Put $A=\mathcal O_{S,s}$, $\mathfrak m=\mathfrak m_s$, and $k=A/\mathfrak m=\kappa(s)$ [def-weil-pbc-module-stalk, def-weil-residue-field]. Form $X=Z\times_S\operatorname{Spec}A$ along the canonical morphism $\operatorname{Spec}A\to S$ [lem-weil-pbc-spec-local-ring-canonical-morphism, def-pc-fibre-product], with projections $h:X\to Z$ and $g:X\to\operatorname{Spec}A$. Write $E_X=h^*E$, $Z_s=Z\times_S\operatorname{Spec}k$, and $E_s=E|_{Z_s}$ [def-pc-module-pullback, def-pc-scheme-fibre]. Let $J=\mathfrak m\mathcal O_X$ [def-nagata-extended-ideal], with powers and quotients as in [def-weil-pbc-coherent-formal-module]. Assume that for every integer $n\geq1$ we have $$H^1\bigl(X,(J^n/J^{n+1})\otimes_{\mathcal O_X}E_X\bigr)=0,$$ where tensor product and cohomology are as in [def-pur-sheaf-tensor-product, pqf-def-cohomology]. Then for every $t\in\Gamma(Z_s,E_s)$ there exist an open neighbourhood $U\subseteq S$ of $s$ and a section $\widetilde t\in\Gamma(f^{-1}U,E|_{f^{-1}U})$ whose pullback to $Z_s$ is $t$.

source.place: Tag 0D2M, lemma-ample-on-fibre, proof: successive quotient exact sequences and image stabilization in degree zero, lines 6047-6089, together with its local-base-change paragraph, lines 5995-6011; the vanishing hypothesis isolates this argument from ampleness.

proof.text: Choose an affine open $V=\operatorname{Spec}R\subseteq S$ containing $s$, corresponding to a prime $\mathfrak p\subset R$. The affine-open Noetherian criterion gives that $R$ is Noetherian. The canonical-local-ring morphism identifies $A=\mathcal O_{S,s}$ with $R_{\mathfrak p}$, so localization permanence makes $A$ Noetherian. Thus $\operatorname{Spec}A$ is locally Noetherian by its one-chart affine cover.

source.place: Tag 0D2M, lemma-ample-on-fibre, first paragraph; Properties Tag 01OW, lemma-locally-Noetherian; Algebra Tag 00FN, lemma-Noetherian-permanence.

proof.text: The base change $g:X\to\operatorname{Spec}A$ is proper. Proper morphisms are of finite type by definition, so the finite-type Noetherian theorem applied to $f$ and $g$ shows that $Z$ and $X$ are locally Noetherian. Set $F=E_X=h^*E$. Pullback preserves invertible modules, so $F$ is invertible. Both $E$ and $F$ are quasi-coherent and locally generated by one element. The coherent finite-type criterion therefore makes $E$ and $F$ coherent on $Z$ and $X$, respectively.

source.place: Tag 0D2M, lemma-ample-on-fibre, local-base-change paragraph; Tag 01XZ, lemma-coherent-Noetherian; Morphisms Tags 01W4 (lemma-base-change-proper) and 01T6 (lemma-finite-type-noetherian).

proof.text: For $n\geq1$ put $Q_n=F/J^nF$ and $K_n=(J^n/J^{n+1})\otimes_{\mathcal O_X}F$. There is a short exact sequence $0\to K_n\to Q_{n+1}\to Q_n\to0$. Indeed the quotient map has kernel $J^nF/J^{n+1}F$. On any open trivializing $F$, the multiplication map $K_n\to J^nF/J^{n+1}F$ becomes the identity of $J^n/J^{n+1}$, so it is an isomorphism. These are the multiplication and quotient maps and hence agree on overlaps. This also identifies $Q_n$ with $(\mathcal O_X/J^n)\otimes F$. Exactness can be checked locally, where it is just $0\to J^n/J^{n+1}\to\mathcal O_X/J^{n+1}\to\mathcal O_X/J^n\to0$.

source.place: Tag 0D2M, lemma-ample-on-fibre, successive quotient exact sequences; local rank-one calculation written out here.

proof.text: Let $i:Z_s\to X$ be the closed-fibre inclusion after the canonical identification $Z_s=X\times_{\operatorname{Spec}A}\operatorname{Spec}k$. This identification follows from the fibre-product universal property, because clause (5) of the canonical-local-ring statement (with $J=\mathfrak m$) says that the morphism $\operatorname{Spec}k\to S$ defining the fibre, induced by $\mathcal O_{S,s}\to\kappa(s)$, is the composite $\operatorname{Spec}k\to\operatorname{Spec}A\to S$ of the quotient closed immersion and the canonical morphism. Apply quotient base change with $K=\mathfrak m$: $i$ is a closed immersion with ideal $J$. The closed-immersion unit quotient theorem gives $Q_1=F/JF\cong i_*i^*F$. Pullback composition identifies $i^*F$ with $E_s$. Consequently $\Gamma(X,Q_1)\cong\Gamma(Z_s,E_s)$, since direct image is evaluation on the inverse image of an open. Under this isomorphism the map from $\Gamma(X,F)$ is exactly restriction to the fibre, by the unit formula of the quotient theorem.

source.place: Tag 01JU, lemma-fibre-product-immersion; Modules Tag 08KS, lemma-i-star-equivalence; Sheaves Tags 0095 and 0096, tensor pullback and its adjunction.

proof.text: For each $n\geq1$, the hypothesis says $H^1(X,K_n)=0$. Apply the section-boundary exactness theorem to the short exact sequence of step 3. The boundary of every section of $Q_n$ is zero, so $\Gamma(X,Q_{n+1})\to\Gamma(X,Q_n)$ is surjective. Given the section $t_1\in\Gamma(X,Q_1)$ corresponding to $t$ in step 4, for every fixed integer $k\geq1$ construct a section $t_k$ mapping to $t_1$ by finite induction: the base $k=1$ is $t_1$ itself, and a preimage of an already constructed $t_k$ under the surjective next transition supplies $t_{k+1}$. The composite quotient map then sends $t_{k+1}$ to $t_1$.

source.place: Tag 0D2M, lemma-ample-on-fibre, long exact sequence and induction paragraph; Cohomology Tag 01DZ for the degree-zero section boundary.

proof.text: Apply the cohomology image-stabilization theorem with Noetherian ring $A$, ideal $\mathfrak m$, proper morphism $g$, coherent module $F$, and degree $p=0$; all hypotheses were verified in steps 1 and 2. It supplies $c\geq0$ such that, writing $H=\Gamma(X,F)$ and $M_n=\Gamma(X,Q_n)$, the image of $M_k\to M_1$ equals the image of $H\to M_1$ whenever $k\geq1+c$. Take $k=1+c$. Step 5 puts $t_1$ in the first image, hence in the second. Choose $u\in\Gamma(X,F)$ mapping to $t_1$. Step 4 says that $u|_{Z_s}=t$. Only this finite level is needed.

source.place: Tag 02OB, lemma-ML-cohomology-powers-ideal, part (3), used in the final degree-zero paragraph of Tag 0D2M.

proof.text: Apply the uncompleted local-stalk comparison to $f$, $E$, $s$, and $p=0$; $f$ is proper, $S$ is locally Noetherian, and $E$ is coherent by step 2. Its local base change $\operatorname{Spec}A\times_SZ$ is $X$ after the canonical swap of fibre-product factors, under which its $g'$ is $h$. It gives an isomorphism $a:(R^0f_*E)_s\xrightarrow{\sim}\Gamma(X,F)$ sending the germ of every neighbourhood section to its pullback to $X$. The degree-zero higher-direct-image identification is $R^0f_*E=f_*E$. Thus $a^{-1}(u)$ is a germ of a section of $f_*E$. By the description of stalk elements, choose an open $U\ni s$ and $\widetilde t\in(f_*E)(U)=\Gamma(f^{-1}U,E|_{f^{-1}U})$ representing this germ. The comparison formula gives $h^*\widetilde t=u$ on $X$ (the canonical local spectrum maps into every neighbourhood of $s$).

source.place: Tag 02OD, lemma-formal-functions-stalk, first half of the proof before completion; Tag 02KH, flat-base-change-cohomology; Cohomology Tag 01E4; Sheaves Tag 0078.

proof.text: Pull the equality $h^*\widetilde t=u$ back along $i:Z_s\to X$. Pullback composition identifies its left side with the pullback of $\widetilde t$ to the original fibre $Z_s$, and its right side is $t$ by step 6. This proves the required neighbourhood lifting.

source.place: Tag 0D2M, lemma-ample-on-fibre, final degree-zero conclusion and initial local-base-change identification.
